evidence_spans: In this paper, the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method.
The microstructural evolution and compositions of the silicide coating under high-temperature oxidation environment were studied.
The results show that the silicide coating could effectively prevent the oxidation of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: There is no scientific consensus regarding the mechanism or phase identity of the 'granular crystals' observed on the MoNbTaTiW RHEA surface at 1300 °C due to a lack of phase composition data in the available literature.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The available evidence only documents the morphological observation (granular crystals) without attempting to correlate this morphology to specific phase transitions (crystallization vs. agglomeration) or chemical decomposition events.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The observation of granular crystals is specifically linked to the 1300 °C oxidation condition in the provided data; no comparative mechanism is offered for 1000 °C in the cited text.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions exist between cited answers because only one answer is present, which explicitly states the mechanism is unknown.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Low. The evidence confirms the presence of granular crystals but provides no data to support or refute the hypothesis of Cr2SiO4 decomposition or specific phase identification.

cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The granular crystals may result from the decomposition of a metastable oxide phase or agglomeration of surface oxides, but this cannot be confirmed without phase identification data.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Perform X-ray diffraction (XRD) or Raman spectroscopy on the surface of the sample oxidized at 1300 °C to definitively identify the crystallographic phases present and determine if Cr2SiO4 is absent or decomposed.
